question: Diabetes mellitus is diagnosed when fasting plasma glucose is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. 126 mg/dL or more

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A fasting plasma glucose of 126 mg/dL or more on two occasions, or a random value of 200 mg/dL with symptoms, confirms diabetes

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 110 mg/dL: 110 mg/dL falls in the impaired fasting glucose range

B — 80 mg/dL: 80 mg/dL is normal

C — 100 mg/dL: 100 mg/dL is normal

⚠️ Exam Trap: Be careful with absolute words such as ALWAYS and NEVER unless the fact is truly absolute.

💎 PNC Pearl: Impaired fasting glucose between 100 and 125 mg/dL identifies prediabetes, which needs lifestyle advice

question: Which laboratory test reflects average blood glucose over the previous two to three months?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. Glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c)

🧠 Clinical Rationale: HbA1c reflects glucose bound to haemoglobin over the lifespan of the red cell, about two to three months

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Urine ketones: Ketones reflect acute fat metabolism

B — Serum creatinine: Creatinine assesses kidney function

D — Fasting plasma glucose: Fasting glucose is a single time point

⚠️ Exam Trap: In FIRST-action questions, identify the life-threatening problem and stabilise or assess before anything else.

💎 PNC Pearl: The usual target for most adults is an HbA1c below 7 per cent

question: A 52-year-old man with type 1 diabetes is prescribed a rapid-acting insulin before meals. When should he be taught to inject it?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. About 15 minutes before the meal

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Rapid-acting insulin is given about 15 minutes before a meal so that its peak matches the glucose rise from the food

🔍 Key Clues: 52-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — At bedtime only: Bedtime-only dosing does not cover meals

C — Once a week: Weekly dosing is impossible for a prandial insulin

D — Two hours after eating: Injection after eating allows early hyperglycaemia

⚠️ Exam Trap: Read the stem twice - one word such as MOST or EXCEPT can reverse the answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: The injection site is rotated to prevent lipohypertrophy

question: A patient on insulin becomes sweaty, tremulous and confused with a glucometer reading of 48 mg/dL. What is the immediate action?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. Give 15 g of fast-acting oral glucose and recheck in 15 minutes

🧠 Clinical Rationale: This is hypoglycaemia, treated with 15 g of rapidly absorbed glucose and a recheck in 15 minutes using the 15-15 rule

🔍 Key Clues: 48 mg/dL

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Give the next insulin dose early: More insulin deepens the hypoglycaemia

C — Give a high-protein meal only: Protein acts too slowly in an emergency

D — Withhold all carbohydrate: Withholding carbohydrate is dangerous

⚠️ Exam Trap: Read the stem twice - one word such as MOST or EXCEPT can reverse the answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: If the patient cannot swallow safely, intravenous dextrose or intramuscular glucagon is used
option_2: Give 15 g of fast-acting oral glucose and recheck in 15 minutes

question: Which triad indicates diabetic ketoacidosis?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. Hyperglycaemia, ketonaemia and metabolic acidosis

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Diabetic ketoacidosis combines hyperglycaemia, ketone production and a high-anion-gap metabolic acidosis

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Hyperglycaemia with metabolic alkalosis: The acidosis is metabolic, not alkalosis

B — Normal glucose with respiratory acidosis: Glucose is raised

D — Hypoglycaemia, ketones and alkalosis: Ketoacidosis is not hypoglycaemic in the classic form

⚠️ Exam Trap: Do not pick an option only because it is familiar - the option that fits the whole stem is the answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: Treatment is fluid, insulin and potassium replacement, because insulin drives potassium into cells

question: A patient with diabetic ketoacidosis has a serum potassium of 3.2 mEq/L. What should be done before or with the insulin infusion?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. Start potassium replacement, because insulin will lower potassium further

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Total body potassium is depleted in ketoacidosis, and insulin shifts potassium into cells, so replacement is started early

🔍 Key Clues: 3.2 mEq/L

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Give bicarbonate: Bicarbonate is not routinely indicated

B — Give insulin first and check potassium later: Insulin alone can precipitate dangerous hypokalaemia and arrhythmia

D — Give a fluid bolus of normal saline only: Fluids are needed but do not correct the potassium

⚠️ Exam Trap: Look for the qualifier (FIRST / BEST / MOST LIKELY) - it decides the answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: Potassium is monitored hourly during treatment
option_2: Give insulin first and check potassium later
option_3: Start potassium replacement, because insulin will lower potassium further
option_4: Give a fluid bolus of normal saline only

question: Hypertension in an adult is generally defined as a sustained blood pressure of:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. 140/90 mmHg or more

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A sustained clinic blood pressure of 140/90 mmHg or more defines hypertension in adults

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 120/70 mmHg: This is a normal reading

C — 100/60 mmHg: This is a normal, even low, reading

D — 130/80 mmHg: This is within the normal range, though many guidelines treat 130/80 as elevated risk

⚠️ Exam Trap: Read the stem twice - one word such as MOST or EXCEPT can reverse the answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: Diagnosis is confirmed by repeated readings rather than a single measurement

question: Which lifestyle measure lowers blood pressure most effectively?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. Reducing dietary sodium and weight

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Sodium restriction, weight loss, exercise and reduced alcohol lower blood pressure

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Drinking more coffee: Excess caffeine can raise blood pressure

B — Increasing salt intake: More salt raises blood pressure

C — Bed rest: Bed rest does not treat chronic hypertension

⚠️ Exam Trap: Look for the qualifier (FIRST / BEST / MOST LIKELY) - it decides the answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: Lifestyle change complements, and sometimes delays the need for, drug therapy

question: Which antihypertensive class is preferred in a patient with both hypertension and diabetic proteinuria?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. Angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors reduce proteinuria and slow diabetic kidney disease

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Thiazide diuretics alone: Thiazides control pressure but do not protect the kidney the same way

B — Beta-blockers alone: Beta-blockers are not first line for this indication

C — Alpha-blockers alone: Alpha-blockers are add-on agents

⚠️ Exam Trap: Be careful with absolute words such as ALWAYS and NEVER unless the fact is truly absolute.

💎 PNC Pearl: Renal function and potassium are checked after starting these drugs

question: A patient has a blood pressure of 210/120 mmHg with headache and blurred vision. What is the priority?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. Urgent controlled reduction of blood pressure and assessment for organ damage

🧠 Clinical Rationale: This is a hypertensive emergency with symptoms, so pressure is lowered in a controlled way while organ damage is assessed

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — Vigorous exercise to lower the pressure: Exercise raises pressure

C — Rapid normalisation to 120/80 within minutes: Too rapid a fall can cause cerebral or myocardial ischaemia

D — Oral therapy and discharge: Discharge is unsafe

⚠️ Exam Trap: Read the stem twice - one word such as MOST or EXCEPT can reverse the answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: The initial aim is to lower the mean arterial pressure by no more than about 25 per cent in the first hour
option_1: Urgent controlled reduction of blood pressure and assessment for organ damage

question: Chronic kidney disease is best defined by:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. Kidney damage or reduced glomerular filtration rate lasting at least three months

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Chronic kidney disease requires a structural or functional abnormality persisting for three months or more

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — An acute rise in creatinine over two days: An acute rise defines acute kidney injury

C — Proteinuria for one week: One week is too short

D — A single high creatinine reading: One reading does not establish chronicity

⚠️ Exam Trap: Do not pick an option only because it is familiar - the option that fits the whole stem is the answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: Estimated glomerular filtration rate and albuminuria together stage the disease
option_1: An acute rise in creatinine over two days
option_2: Kidney damage or reduced glomerular filtration rate lasting at least three months

question: A declining estimated glomerular filtration rate is staged in chronic kidney disease. Which value indicates severe impairment (stage 4)?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. 15–29 mL/min/1.73 m²

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Stage 4 is an estimated glomerular filtration rate of 15 to 29, and stage 5 is below 15, or dialysis-dependent

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — More than 90: Above 90 is normal

B — 30–44: 30 to 44 falls in stage 3b

C — 60–89: 60 to 89 is stage 2

⚠️ Exam Trap: Look for the qualifier (FIRST / BEST / MOST LIKELY) - it decides the answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: Stage determines drug dosing, diet and referral for renal replacement

question: Which dietary change is usually advised in advanced chronic kidney disease?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. Restricted protein, potassium and phosphate with controlled sodium

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Limiting protein, potassium and phosphate eases the burden on failing kidneys and helps control complications

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Liberal potassium-rich foods: Potassium-rich foods risk hyperkalaemia

B — Extra phosphate supplements: Phosphate supplements worsen renal bone disease

C — Very high protein intake: A high protein load worsens uraemia

⚠️ Exam Trap: Do not pick an option only because it is familiar - the option that fits the whole stem is the answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: A renal dietitian tailors the plan to each patient's stage and labs
option_4: Restricted protein, potassium and phosphate with controlled sodium

question: Anaemia in chronic kidney disease is mainly caused by:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. Reduced erythropoietin production by the failing kidney

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The kidney makes erythropoietin, so falling production reduces red cell synthesis; iron and erythropoietin therapy are used

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Iron overload: Iron deficiency, not overload, is common

C — Vitamin C deficiency: Vitamin C deficiency causes scurvy, not this anaemia

D — Increased red cell production: Production falls rather than rises

⚠️ Exam Trap: Look for the qualifier (FIRST / BEST / MOST LIKELY) - it decides the answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: Iron stores are checked before starting erythropoietin to ensure an adequate response
option_2: Reduced erythropoietin production by the failing kidney

question: A patient with advanced chronic kidney disease has potassium 6.2 mEq/L with tall T waves. Which action is most urgent?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. Give intravenous calcium gluconate to protect the heart, then shift and remove potassium

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Calcium stabilises the myocardium immediately, and further measures shift potassium into cells and remove it from the body

🔍 Key Clues: 6.2 mEq/L

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Give a potassium-sparing diuretic: Potassium-sparing diuretics raise potassium further

B — Give a potassium-rich diet: Potassium-rich food worsens the level

D — Withhold all treatment and observe: Observation risks arrhythmia

⚠️ Exam Trap: Be careful with absolute words such as ALWAYS and NEVER unless the fact is truly absolute.

💎 PNC Pearl: Dialysis is arranged if conservative measures fail
option_3: Give intravenous calcium gluconate to protect the heart, then shift and remove potassium

question: Which symptom is typical of left-sided heart failure?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. Breathlessness on exertion with orthopnoea

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Left-sided failure causes pulmonary congestion with exertional dyspnoea, orthopnoea and paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnoea

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — Raised jugular venous pressure only: Raised jugular venous pressure is a right-sided sign

C — Ankle oedema only: Ankle oedema is more typical of right-sided failure

D — Painful, enlarged liver only: Liver enlargement and tenderness are right-sided signs

⚠️ Exam Trap: In FIRST-action questions, identify the life-threatening problem and stabilise or assess before anything else.

💎 PNC Pearl: Many patients have both sides affected, so signs overlap

question: Which nursing position relieves breathlessness in a patient with pulmonary congestion?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. High Fowler's with the legs dependent

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Sitting up with the legs dependent reduces venous return and eases the work of breathing

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Prone position: The prone position is not used for this purpose

B — Trendelenburg position: A head-down position increases venous return and worsens congestion

C — Flat supine position: Lying flat worsens congestion and breathlessness

⚠️ Exam Trap: In FIRST-action questions, identify the life-threatening problem and stabilise or assess before anything else.

💎 PNC Pearl: Oxygen and diuretic therapy are given as prescribed alongside positioning

question: A patient with heart failure has gained 3 kg in two days with worsening ankle oedema and basal crackles. Which action is appropriate?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. Restrict fluid and salt, record daily weight and report for diuretic review

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Rapid weight gain with oedema and crackles signals fluid overload, so intake is controlled, daily weight is charted and the team reviews diuretics

🔍 Key Clues: 3 kg

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Restrict all activity permanently: Graded activity is encouraged once stable

B — Increase salt intake: Salt retention worsens congestion

D — Encourage extra oral fluids: Extra fluid worsens overload

⚠️ Exam Trap: Be careful with absolute words such as ALWAYS and NEVER unless the fact is truly absolute.

💎 PNC Pearl: Daily weight is the most useful indicator of fluid balance in heart failure
option_3: Restrict fluid and salt, record daily weight and report for diuretic review

question: Why is a daily weight recorded for a patient with heart failure?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. It detects fluid retention before it becomes clinically obvious

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A gain of about 1 kg corresponds to roughly a litre of retained fluid and gives early warning

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — It measures body fat: Weight does not measure fat accurately in this setting

C — It replaces blood pressure monitoring: It does not replace blood pressure checks

D — It assesses muscle strength: It is not a strength measure

⚠️ Exam Trap: Read the stem twice - one word such as MOST or EXCEPT can reverse the answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: Weight is taken at the same time each day, ideally before breakfast, with the same clothing
option_2: It detects fluid retention before it becomes clinically obvious

question: A patient with diabetes is taught about foot care. Which advice is correct?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. Inspect the feet daily and wear well-fitting, closed footwear

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Daily inspection and proper footwear prevent unnoticed injury in a foot with reduced sensation

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — Walk barefoot at home: Barefoot walking risks injury

C — Warm the feet with a hot-water bottle: Reduced sensation makes burns from hot water likely

D — Cut corns with a blade: Self-cutting corns can cause ulcers

⚠️ Exam Trap: Be careful with absolute words such as ALWAYS and NEVER unless the fact is truly absolute.

💎 PNC Pearl: Neuropathy and poor circulation make the diabetic foot vulnerable, so early reporting of any break in the skin matters
option_1: Inspect the feet daily and wear well-fitting, closed footwear
option_3: Warm the feet with a hot-water bottle

question: Which finding suggests early diabetic nephropathy?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. Persistent albuminuria with a rising blood pressure

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Microalbuminuria is the earliest marker of diabetic kidney disease and predicts progression

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Frank haematuria: Frank haematuria suggests another cause

C — A single high fasting glucose: A single glucose reading only confirms diabetes

D — Polyuria with normal albumin: Polyuria without albuminuria is not nephropathy

⚠️ Exam Trap: In FIRST-action questions, identify the life-threatening problem and stabilise or assess before anything else.

💎 PNC Pearl: Good glucose and blood pressure control slows nephropathy
option_2: Persistent albuminuria with a rising blood pressure

question: Which instruction is important for a patient starting a diuretic for hypertension?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. Take it in the morning and rise slowly because of possible postural drop

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A morning dose reduces night-time urination, and rising slowly prevents dizziness from postural hypotension

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — Stop the drug when the pressure is normal: Therapy is long term and must not be stopped without advice

C — Skip the evening dose only: Consistency matters more than skipping

D — Take it at bedtime with a large meal: Bedtime dosing disturbs sleep

⚠️ Exam Trap: Read the stem twice - one word such as MOST or EXCEPT can reverse the answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: Electrolytes such as potassium are monitored during diuretic therapy
option_1: Take it in the morning and rise slowly because of possible postural drop
option_2: Stop the drug when the pressure is normal
option_4: Take it at bedtime with a large meal

question: Which change requires immediate reporting in a patient with heart failure on digoxin?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. A pulse of 52/min with nausea and visual disturbance

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Bradycardia with nausea and visual changes suggests digoxin toxicity, so the drug is held and reported

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — A dry cough: A dry cough is associated with angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors rather than digoxin

B — Mild constipation: Mild constipation is not the typical concern

C — A pulse of 76/min: A pulse of 76/min is normal

⚠️ Exam Trap: Be careful with absolute words such as ALWAYS and NEVER unless the fact is truly absolute.

💎 PNC Pearl: Digoxin levels and potassium are checked because hypokalaemia increases toxicity
option_4: A pulse of 52/min with nausea and visual disturbance

question: Which insulin type has the fastest onset of action?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. Rapid-acting insulin such as lispro

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Rapid-acting analogues act within about 15 minutes and peak in one to two hours

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — Isophane (NPH) insulin: Isophane is intermediate acting

C — Long-acting glargine: Glargine is a basal insulin with a flat profile

D — Premixed insulin: Premixed insulins combine rapid and intermediate components

⚠️ Exam Trap: Look for the qualifier (FIRST / BEST / MOST LIKELY) - it decides the answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: The onset, peak and duration guide the timing of meals and monitoring

question: The replacement of one mature cell type by another within the same tissue is called:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. Metaplasia

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Metaplasia is a reversible change in which one mature cell type is replaced by another, often from chronic irritation

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Atrophy: Atrophy is shrinkage in cell size

C — Dysplasia: Dysplasia is disordered growth with abnormal cells

D — Hypertrophy: Hypertrophy is an increase in cell size

⚠️ Exam Trap: Distinguish acute from chronic, and reversible from irreversible, before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: Smoking causes squamous metaplasia in the airways

question: Programmed cell death that does not cause inflammation is called:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. Apoptosis

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Apoptosis is a regulated, energy-dependent removal of cells that leaves the membrane intact and does not provoke inflammation

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Coagulation: Coagulation is a type of necrosis

B — Necrosis: Necrosis causes inflammation and membrane rupture

D — Gangrene: Gangrene is tissue death with putrefaction

⚠️ Exam Trap: Distinguish acute from chronic, and reversible from irreversible, before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: Loss of apoptosis contributes to cancer growth

question: A granuloma is best described as:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. A focal collection of activated macrophages, often with giant cells

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Granulomas are aggregates of activated macrophages and giant cells formed in chronic inflammation such as tuberculosis

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — A collection of red blood cells: Red cell collections are haematomas

B — A fluid-filled cyst: A cyst is a fluid-filled cavity

D — A malignant tumour: A granuloma is not malignant

⚠️ Exam Trap: Distinguish acute from chronic, and reversible from irreversible, before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: Caseating granulomas are typical of tuberculosis
option_3: A focal collection of activated macrophages, often with giant cells

question: Free radical injury contributes to cell death mainly by:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. Peroxidation of membrane lipids

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Free radicals damage lipids, proteins and DNA, and lipid peroxidation disrupts the cell membrane

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — Increasing intracellular ATP: Free radicals lower rather than raise ATP

C — Strengthening the cell membrane: They weaken membranes

D — Reducing oxidative stress: They increase oxidative stress

⚠️ Exam Trap: Distinguish acute from chronic, and reversible from irreversible, before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: Antioxidants such as glutathione protect the cell

question: In a balanced diet, carbohydrates should provide approximately what share of daily energy?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. 50–60%

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Carbohydrates usually supply 50 to 60 per cent of energy, mostly from complex and fibre-rich sources

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 80–90%: 80 to 90 per cent is excessive

B — 0%: Carbohydrate is the main energy source

D — 5–10%: 5 to 10 per cent is closer to the fat or added-sugar allowance

⚠️ Exam Trap: Separate the deficiency disease from its dietary source - exams mix the two.

💎 PNC Pearl: Fibre-rich carbohydrate improves glycaemic control and bowel health

question: Which dietary advice best supports glycaemic control in diabetes?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. Regular meals with complex carbohydrate, high fibre and limited refined sugar

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Regular balanced meals with complex carbohydrate, fibre and limited refined sugar smooth out glucose swings

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — Frequent sugary snacks: Sugary snacks cause spikes

C — Skipping breakfast daily: Skipping breakfast risks hypoglycaemia and overeating later

D — A diet of only fruit juices: Fruit juice has a high sugar load

⚠️ Exam Trap: Separate the deficiency disease from its dietary source - exams mix the two.

💎 PNC Pearl: The diet is matched to the insulin regimen and activity
option_1: Regular meals with complex carbohydrate, high fibre and limited refined sugar

question: A patient with hypertension is advised to reduce sodium. Which change helps most?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. Avoiding pickles, papad and processed foods, and not adding table salt

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Most dietary sodium comes from added salt and processed foods, so cutting these lowers intake substantially

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Drinking more water: Extra water does not reduce sodium load

B — Increasing milk intake: Milk is not a major sodium source

D — Eating more canned soup: Canned soup is very high in sodium

⚠️ Exam Trap: Separate the deficiency disease from its dietary source - exams mix the two.

💎 PNC Pearl: Reading food labels for sodium content supports the change
option_3: Avoiding pickles, papad and processed foods, and not adding table salt

question: Why is protein intake restricted in advanced chronic kidney disease not yet on dialysis?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. To reduce the production of nitrogenous waste such as urea

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Metabolising protein produces urea and other nitrogenous waste that the failing kidney cannot clear, so intake is moderated with adequate energy

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — To reduce blood pressure only: The main purpose is to control uraemia

B — To increase urine output: Protein restriction does not increase urine output

C — To raise the potassium level: It may reduce rather than raise potassium

⚠️ Exam Trap: Separate the deficiency disease from its dietary source - exams mix the two.

💎 PNC Pearl: Once dialysis starts, protein needs rise again because dialysis removes amino acids
option_4: To reduce the production of nitrogenous waste such as urea

question: Which hormone raises blood glucose by promoting glycogenolysis?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. Glucagon

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Glucagon from pancreatic alpha cells raises glucose by stimulating glycogen breakdown and gluconeogenesis

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Thyroxine: Thyroxine raises metabolic rate rather than acting as the main glucose-raising hormone

C — Insulin: Insulin lowers blood glucose

D — Calcitonin: Calcitonin lowers serum calcium

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: The balance of insulin and glucagon maintains glucose within a narrow range

question: Which lipid fraction is known as the good cholesterol because it removes cholesterol from tissues?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. High-density lipoprotein

🧠 Clinical Rationale: High-density lipoprotein transports cholesterol from tissues back to the liver, which protects against atherosclerosis

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Very low-density lipoprotein: Very low-density lipoprotein carries triglycerides

C — Low-density lipoprotein: Low-density lipoprotein deposits cholesterol in arteries

D — Chylomicron: Chylomicrons carry dietary fat

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: A higher high-density lipoprotein and lower low-density lipoprotein reduce cardiovascular risk

question: The five rights of medication administration include all of the following except:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. The right to refuse the drug for any reason by the nurse's choice

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The rights are patient, drug, dose, route and time; a nurse cannot unilaterally refuse to give a prescribed drug, though genuine safety concerns are reported

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — The right patient: The right patient is fundamental

B — The right dose: The right dose prevents overdose

C — The right route: The right route prevents wrong-site administration

⚠️ Exam Trap: Remember that delegation transfers the task but never the accountability.

💎 PNC Pearl: Some list additional rights such as documentation and the right to refuse by the patient
option_4: The right to refuse the drug for any reason by the nurse's choice

question: The numeric rating scale for pain asks the patient to rate pain from:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. 0 (no pain) to 10 (worst pain imaginable)

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The numeric rating scale runs from 0 for no pain to 10 for the worst pain imaginable

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — 0 to 1: 0 to 1 gives almost no discrimination

C — 100 to 200: 100 to 200 is not a standard scale

D — 1 to 3 only: The range is wider than 1 to 3

⚠️ Exam Trap: In procedure questions choose the step that protects the patient first - safety before comfort and speed.

💎 PNC Pearl: Pain is reassessed after every intervention to judge its effect

question: A nurse is about to change a wound dressing. Which action maintains sterility?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. Keep the sterile field above waist level and never turn the back on it

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A sterile field is kept above waist level and in view so that contamination is noticed at once

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Let the sterile drape touch the uniform: Contact with clothing contaminates the field

B — Reach across the field with a bare hand: A bare hand contaminates sterile items

D — Use the same gauze for cleaning and covering: The same gauze spreads organisms back to the wound

⚠️ Exam Trap: In procedure questions choose the step that protects the patient first - safety before comfort and speed.

💎 PNC Pearl: Any item touching a non-sterile surface is discarded
option_1: Let the sterile drape touch the uniform
option_2: Reach across the field with a bare hand
option_3: Keep the sterile field above waist level and never turn the back on it
option_4: Use the same gauze for cleaning and covering

question: Which principle of body mechanics protects the nurse during patient handling?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. Keep the load close to the body and bend at the knees

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Keeping the load close and using the leg muscles reduces the strain on the spine

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Lift with the back muscles in a stooped position: Lifting with a stooped back strains the lumbar spine

B — Hold the load away from the body: Holding the load away increases the lever arm and the load on the spine

C — Twist the trunk while lifting: Twisting while lifting is a common cause of back injury

⚠️ Exam Trap: In procedure questions choose the step that protects the patient first - safety before comfort and speed.

💎 PNC Pearl: Assistive devices and help from colleagues should be used for heavy patients
option_1: Lift with the back muscles in a stooped position
option_2: Hold the load away from the body
option_4: Keep the load close to the body and bend at the knees

question: For a clean-catch midstream urine specimen, the nurse should instruct the patient to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. Clean the genital area and collect the middle part of the stream in a sterile container

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Cleansing and collecting the midstream portion minimise contamination from the surrounding skin

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Collect urine from the drainage bag: Bag urine is contaminated and stagnant

B — Use a non-sterile container: A sterile container is required

D — Collect the first part of the stream: The first portion contains urethral flora

⚠️ Exam Trap: In procedure questions choose the step that protects the patient first - safety before comfort and speed.

💎 PNC Pearl: The specimen is sent to the laboratory promptly or refrigerated
option_3: Clean the genital area and collect the middle part of the stream in a sterile container
option_4: Collect the first part of the stream

question: When restraints are used, which action is essential?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. Check the limb circulation and remove the restraint at regular intervals

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Circulation, sensation and skin are checked frequently and the restraint is released regularly to prevent injury

question: A convex lens is used to correct which eye defect?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. Hypermetropia

🧠 Clinical Rationale: In hypermetropia the eye focuses images behind the retina, and a convex lens converges the light earlier so that near objects become clear

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — Colour blindness: Colour blindness cannot be corrected with a lens

C — Astigmatism only: Astigmatism is corrected with a cylindrical lens

D — Myopia: Myopia is corrected with a concave lens

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: Hypermetropia means near objects appear blurred while distant vision is relatively preserved

question: The normal number of permanent teeth in an adult is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. 32

🧠 Clinical Rationale: An adult normally has 32 permanent teeth, including four wisdom teeth

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 36: 36 is too many

B — 20: 20 is the number of primary or milk teeth

C — 28: 28 is the count before the wisdom teeth erupt

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: Oral hygiene prevents caries and periodontal disease

question: The acid present in vinegar is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. Acetic acid

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Vinegar is a dilute solution of acetic acid, used in cooking and as a mild preservative

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Sulphuric acid: Sulphuric acid is a strong mineral acid

B — Citric acid: Citric acid is found in citrus fruits

C — Lactic acid: Lactic acid is found in curd and sore muscles

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: A weak acid dissociates only partially in water

question: What is 20% of 350?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. 70

🧠 Method: Twenty per cent of 350 is 0.20 × 350 = 70

⚡ Fast Approach: Break the percentage into easy parts (10 percent, 5 percent, 1 percent) and add them.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 7: 7 is 2 per cent

C — 105: 105 is 30 per cent

D — 35: 35 is 10 per cent of 350

⚠️ Exam Trap: Read the stem twice - one word such as MOST or EXCEPT can reverse the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: To find a percentage, change it to a decimal and multiply

question: What is the average of 18, 22, 30 and 34?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. 26

🧠 Method: The sum is 104 and there are four numbers, so the average is 26

⚡ Fast Approach: Total = average x number of items. Find the total first, then subtract the known values.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 24: 24 would need a sum of 96

B — 30: 30 ignores the lower values

C — 28: 28 would need a sum of 112

⚠️ Exam Trap: In FIRST-action questions, identify the life-threatening problem and stabilise or assess before anything else.

💎 PNC Trick: Average equals the sum divided by the count

question: Two numbers are in the ratio 4 : 7 and their sum is 88. What is the larger number?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. 56

🧠 Method: The total of the parts is 11, so one part is 8 and the larger number is 7 × 8 = 56

⚡ Fast Approach: Add the parts to get the total number of parts, then find the value of one part.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 49: 49 does not fit the parts

B — 32: 32 is the smaller number

D — 44: 44 is half the sum

⚠️ Exam Trap: Read the stem twice - one word such as MOST or EXCEPT can reverse the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: Add the ratio terms to find the value of one part

question: An article sold for ₹460 at a loss of 8% had a cost price of:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. ₹500

🧠 Method: If the selling price is 92 per cent of the cost price, the cost is 460 ÷ 0.92 = ₹500

⚡ Fast Approach: Profit percent is always on the cost price, loss percent also on the cost price.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — ₹450: ₹450 would give a profit

C — ₹480: ₹480 would give a smaller loss

D — ₹520: ₹520 would give a profit

⚠️ Exam Trap: In FIRST-action questions, identify the life-threatening problem and stabilise or assess before anything else.

💎 PNC Trick: Selling price equals cost price minus the loss

question: If 6 workers can complete a task in 12 days, how long will 9 workers take at the same rate?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. 8 days

🧠 Method: Worker-days are constant at 6 × 12 = 72, so 72 ÷ 9 = 8 days

⚡ Fast Approach: Combine rates as 1/A + 1/B, then invert to get the number of days.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — 9 days: 9 days is more than the correct time

C — 18 days: 18 days wrongly doubles the time

D — 6 days: 6 days is shorter than the correct time

⚠️ Exam Trap: Be careful with absolute words such as ALWAYS and NEVER unless the fact is truly absolute.

💎 PNC Trick: In inverse proportion the product stays constant

question: In what time will ₹4,000 yield ₹720 as simple interest at 6% per annum?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. 3 years

🧠 Method: Time equals interest ÷ (principal × rate ÷ 100), so 720 ÷ 240 = 3 years

⚡ Fast Approach: SI = P x R x T / 100. Keep T in years - convert months to a fraction.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — 2 years: 2 years would give ₹480

C — 4 years: 4 years would give ₹960

D — 5 years: 5 years would give ₹1,200

⚠️ Exam Trap: Do not pick an option only because it is familiar - the option that fits the whole stem is the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: Rearrange the simple-interest formula to find the unknown term

question: A cyclist covers 45 km in 2 hours 30 minutes. What is the average speed?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. 18 km/h

🧠 Method: Two hours thirty minutes is 2.5 hours, and 45 ÷ 2.5 = 18 km/h

⚡ Fast Approach: Average speed = total distance / total time - never the mean of the two speeds.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 15 km/h: 15 km/h would need 3 hours

C — 20 km/h: 20 km/h would need 2.25 hours

D — 22.5 km/h: 22.5 km/h is 45 ÷ 2

⚠️ Exam Trap: In FIRST-action questions, identify the life-threatening problem and stabilise or assess before anything else.

💎 PNC Trick: Convert minutes into hours before dividing

question: Find the next number: 7, 14, 21, 28, __
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. 35

🧠 Method: The series is the multiples of 7, so the next is 35

⚡ Fast Approach: Check the differences first, then squares, cubes or multiplication.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 36: 36 is not a multiple of 7

B — 34: 34 is not a multiple of 7

D — 32: 32 is not a multiple of 7

⚠️ Exam Trap: Look for the qualifier (FIRST / BEST / MOST LIKELY) - it decides the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: Check whether the terms are multiples of a fixed number

question: Kidney is to nephron as lung is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. Alveolus

🧠 Method: The nephron is the functional unit of the kidney, so the alveolus is the functional unit of the lung

⚡ Fast Approach: State the relationship in words first, then look for the same relationship.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Diaphragm: The diaphragm is the main muscle of breathing

C — Bronchus: The bronchus is a conducting airway

D — Trachea: The trachea is the windpipe

⚠️ Exam Trap: Do not pick an option only because it is familiar - the option that fits the whole stem is the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: Match the functional-unit relationship in the pair

question: If TREE is coded as 20-18-5-5 using letter positions, how is LEAF coded?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. 12-5-1-6

🧠 Method: L is 12, E is 5, A is 1 and F is 6, giving 12-5-1-6

⚡ Fast Approach: Compare the first and last letters of the given pair to find the shift.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 12-4-1-6: 4 stands for D, not E

B — 11-5-1-6: 11 stands for K, not L

D — 12-5-1-5: 5 stands for E, not F

⚠️ Exam Trap: Do not pick an option only because it is familiar - the option that fits the whole stem is the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: Confirm the letter positions of the first and last letters

question: A person faces north, turns 90° to the right, then 90° to the left. Which direction is the person facing now?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. North

🧠 Method: Turning right from north gives east, and turning left from east returns to north

⚡ Fast Approach: Draw a small diagram - each turn changes the direction by a fixed angle.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — West: West is not reached

C — East: East is the intermediate direction

D — South: South would require two more turns

⚠️ Exam Trap: Read the stem twice - one word such as MOST or EXCEPT can reverse the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: Track each turn on a simple compass sketch

question: All doctors are graduates. All graduates are literate. Which conclusion definitely follows?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. All doctors are literate

🧠 Method: If every doctor is a graduate and every graduate is literate, then every doctor is literate

⚡ Fast Approach: Draw the circles of the given sets and see which conclusion is certain.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — No doctor is literate: It contradicts the premises

B — Some doctors are not literate: It contradicts the premises

C — All literate people are doctors: This reverses the chain

⚠️ Exam Trap: Look for the qualifier (FIRST / BEST / MOST LIKELY) - it decides the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: A chain of universal statements transfers the property to the first group

question: P is Q's brother. R is Q's mother. How is P related to R?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. Son

🧠 Method: P is the brother of Q, and R is Q's mother, so P is also R's son

⚡ Fast Approach: Draw the family tree and mark the given relations before answering.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — Nephew: A nephew would be the child of a sibling

C — Uncle: An uncle is a sibling of a parent

D — Brother: A brother would be a sibling of R

⚠️ Exam Trap: Look for the qualifier (FIRST / BEST / MOST LIKELY) - it decides the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: Siblings share the same mother, so P is R's son

question: All bank employees can use the staff canteen. Mr Sen can use the staff canteen. Which conclusion is valid?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. No certain conclusion about Mr Sen's employment can be drawn

🧠 Method: The rule is one-directional, so other people may also be allowed to use the canteen and Mr Sen's employment cannot be inferred

⚡ Fast Approach: Substitute into the standard formula and keep the units consistent.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Mr Sen is definitely not a bank employee: Employment remains possible

B — Mr Sen is definitely a bank employee: This commits the fallacy of affirming the consequent

C — Only bank employees can use the canteen: This reverses the rule

⚠️ Exam Trap: Look for the qualifier (FIRST / BEST / MOST LIKELY) - it decides the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: "If A then B" never allows you to conclude A from B
option_1: Mr Sen is definitely not a bank employee
option_2: Mr Sen is definitely a bank employee
option_3: Only bank employees can use the canteen
option_4: No certain conclusion about Mr Sen's employment can be drawn
